newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Moskvich to get Renault engines.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Moskvich to get Renault engines.

text.p: Russian car maker AO Moskvich, recently threatened with bankruptcy, will receive a shipment of engines from France's Renault in August, director Ruben Asatryan said on Tuesday.

A spokesman for Renault in France confirmed that his company would send Moskvich 2,500 to 3,000 2.0 litre engines, modifications of those used for Renault's own mid-size Laguna and Megane models, in August or September.
Asatryan told a news conference in Moscow that Moskvich planned to assemble over 2,000 Moskvich cars with the new engines and 100 Renault Meganes in September.
The Renault spokesman was unable to comment on Moskvich plans to assemble the French-made cars.
"The first pre-payment has already been made," Asatryan said. The Renault spokesman also said the 2,500 to 3,000 engines had been paid for.

Renault and Moskvich agreed a 40,000-engine contract for one year in February 1996 but Moskvich has had difficulty securing a necessary credit line. It was unclear whether the credit line was already in place.
Moskvich production is extremely low but the company hopes to ramp up to 4,000 cars per month by the end of the year thanks to a credit plan with bank KB Probiznesbank.
